name: SenseShapes
summary: Invisible or visible volumes (cones, spheres) attached to the head and hand record which objects pass through them over time; these rankings are fused with speech and gesture to work out which object the user means.
howItWorks: SenseShapes are regions of interest (cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres) attached to tracked body parts: e.g. an invisible cone from the head approximating gaze, and a visible pointing cone from the hand. Every frame the system logs which objects intersect each shape, and for a time window it ranks candidates by time inside the region, stability (how often they enter and leave), visibility (share of an off-screen object buffer rendered from the cone apex) and closeness to the cone centre. A multimodal integrator fuses these n-best object lists with n-best speech and 3D gesture (point, push, twist, rotate) hypotheses, so each modality can correct the others (mutual disambiguation); e.g. 'make that blue' while pointing, or 'make the table red' while just looking. In a pilot (6 users, VR interior-design room with 50 objects, magnetic trackers), mutual disambiguation accounted for 46% of correct interpretations, though object identification from gesture alone was right only 52% of the time.

relationships.note: Uses pointing cones, ranked over time rather than at one instant.
